output.scope_note: The paper is a first-principles study of Li-Nb-O and Li-Ta-O coating materials, and it quotes several Li-ion conductivity values from earlier experimental work, so it reports conductivities of solid Li-ion conductors, although none are newly measured here.

records.evidence_quote: Albeit with much lower Li-ion conductivities (<10−12 S cm−1 at 400K) and exceedingly high migration barriers (1.16–1.33 eV), 13,14 crystalline LiNbO3 and LiTaO3 coatings
records.notes: Value is an upper bound ('<'), attributed to refs 13,14 (earlier work). The 1.16–1.33 eV values are migration barriers, not activation energies of conductivity, so activation_energy_eV is left null. 400 K converted to 126.85 °C.

records.evidence_quote: materials with high ionic conductivities (∼10−5 –10−6 S cm−1 at room temperature)
records.notes: Range given in the paper, not a single value. The sentence cites refs 10–12 for these materials, so this is literature_cited. Not a specific composition.

records.material_as_written: nanocrystalline LiNbO3 and LiTaO3 (from high-energy ball milling)
records.evidence_quote: Previous reports 13,14 suggested that highly defective nanocrystalline LiNbO3 and LiTaO3 (from high-energy ball milling) containing amorphous-like components exhibit roomtemperature Li-ion conductivities (∼10−6 S cm−1 )
records.notes: Value attributed to previous reports 13,14, so literature_cited. Synthesis route is the one described for those cited materials, not for this paper's work.
